pages.title: About Face
pages.text: Hello. In society, I am paid to conduct research in experimental neutrino physics by Brookhaven National Lab as part of the Electronic Detector Group in the Physics Department . What you may read here are my own representations. Financial considerations aside, I also happen to enjoy this activity particularly as it pertains to developing and applying various computing software and hardware tools. The challenges these tools pose are interesting to me in their own right but my underlying motivation is to help bring us more fundamental understanding of our universe. And toward that end neutrinos provide sharp though even challenging tools. My contributions to this combination to turning bytes into neutrinos may be roughly categorized as: offline software The center of this effort is in EDG’s subgroup known as Wire-Cell and expressions in the form of suites of simulation, data processing and reconstruction software in prototype and toolkit form. More broadly I am involved in general offline software ecosystems including that for DUNE . machine learning I started and continue to participate in development of a novel “artificial intelligence / machine learning” technique which we have named LS4GAN . It is a method to strike at a core AI/ML problem: training a network on simulated data while applying it to perform inference on data from real detectors all the while knowing that these are two different data domains. online software I contribute to development of data acquisition software for the DUNE experiment particularly in the area of configuration management with my moo schema based code generator playing an important role. Throughout this web site you may find blog posts or longer articles that give details on these and other activities. More meta details may be found in the about this site page.

pages.title: About this site
pages.text: In which I give the requisite grandiloquent soliloquy about how this site is made. Purpose and intent Many times in the past I have attempted to make a “web site” that is somehow about me . This is the latest. Time will tell if it survives. This site is intended as an outlet for: Provide browsable, searchable collection of talks . Distribution of Totally Meaningful Parts ( tmp ). I will sometimes answer technical questions in a blog post, in a longer and potentially revised article (such as howido ) or with LLM-assistance an artifact . Some such things may also land in Wire-Cell News posts. I may occasiounly put a short non sequitur or a “today I learned” in notes . Organization Following Hugo nomenclature the site is organized first by sections . Sections are interpreted as a type or a form of page. The following sections may be found: posts short “blog” entries, unlikely to (but may) see updates. articles long form on a topic and potentially updated over time. talks slides from presentations I have given, each with a summary. notes things likely more interesting to myself than others which is meant to summarize or simply mark some occurrence. projects one page for each software project I develop or contribute to. experiments one page for each experiment I collaborate on. about meta descriptions (ie, this page). Pages are further labeled by taxonomies . Hugo provides these with no assumed interpretation and so these are taken: categories A limited number of general descriptors defined in a top-down manner. These label the basic topical subject of the page independent of its section. tags Numerous, unbound set of detailed descriptors defined in a bottom-up manner as pages are written. These label aspects of the content regardless of category or section. groups and topics The group (eg, an experiment or project) to which a talk was given and the topic of the talk. Each project and experiment page automatically lists the pages whose tag, group or topic matches it. The search page searches all pages from within your browser. The site is served in two places. My personal site holds pages of personal interest and those of general interest. My work site holds pages of work interest, those of general interest and the talks. Some pages are only readable by members of a group. Tech This site uses GNU Emacs Org Mode with ox-hugo to make content for Hugo . See howido if interested in details of my personal computing configuration. The org source of each page is linked from it (“org source”). Writing, building and deploying the site is done with myweb , a small command line tool I wrote that keeps the sources in a DataLad dataset, sorts pages to each site by their audience and deploys each by rsync or git. Though not likely interesting to humans, the exported HTML of the personal site lands in this repo .

pages.title: How to use myweb and drop
pages.text: The model The site source is the DataLad dataset ~/keep/web . Each page is an item : a directory (a Hugo page bundle) in a taxon such as posts , articles , notes , projects or experiments . The item holds its org source and any images or files it uses. A target is one place the site is deployed: local ( ~/public_html ), github (GitHub Pages) and work (hierocles). Taxa and targets are defined in ~/keep/web/myweb.toml ; host specifics, such as where each target goes, are in ~/.config/myweb/config.toml . An item is named by its slug, taxon/slug or a path. Write Create a draft, then open it: myweb new posts "A Title" -t emacs -t org myweb new notes "TIL" -m "One line is a whole note." myweb new articles "Long Thing" -d 2026-12-31 # TODO with deadline, in org-agenda myweb edit a-title edit opens a browser on a local preview that includes drafts, and the org file in your editor: editor in config.toml , else $EDITOR , else $VISUAL . When you quit the editor the item is exported and the preview shows it. If the editor is emacsclient , the file opens in your running Emacs (through [emacs] client ) and every save re-exports, so the preview follows as you write. See what is in progress, and check an item before publishing: myweb status # drafts: deadline, TODO, words, figures myweb status -a -x posts myweb check a-title # export, build, check links; report also in .check.txt Linking: To Write a section or page of this site [[/posts][posts]] , [[/articles/howido][howido]] a path no org file makes [[site:artifacts/][artifacts]] an area only some sites have its full URL, eg [[https://www.phy.bnl.gov/~bviren/tmp/][tmp]] a file in the item [[file:fig.svg]] A bare [[posts/]] fails the export: org looks for a local file or heading. Who sees an item Set in the item's org header: Keyword Values Effect #+audience: personal · work · both personal goes only to github, work only to work, both to each (local gets all) #+visibility: public · unlisted · protected unlisted and protected are never listed; protected needs a password and never goes to github #+access: a realm, eg edg which password a protected item needs (the target's realms ) Tags ( #+hugo_tags: ) also place an item on a project or experiment page whose slug matches, eg tag dune lists it on DUNE . Publish myweb publish a-title This clears the draft flag, exports, commits, updates the item's version stamp (and tags the revision, in a taxon with tag = true ), then deploys to the publish_targets of your config. --no-deploy stops after recording; -T work picks the targets. Deploy myweb build work # build and check only, into ~/.cache/myweb/stage/work myweb deploy local # build, then send myweb deploy github work myweb deploy -a # every publish_target Each target is sent by whatever it sets: dest (a local directory), rsync (a host:path/ ), git (a repository whose branch gets the build as one commit). Paths in keep , such as tmp/ , are never touched. A build fails, sending nothing, if an excluded or protected page leaked into it. To deploy without asking: myweb setup systemd -T work (or cron , git ); --print shows what it would install. Talks A talk is a directory ~/keep/talks/<group>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<topic>/ holding its sources, its PDF and a talk.json . Each becomes a page under talks/ on the next build. A command names a talk by that path, by its topic alone if no other talk shares it, or by a file path. Start a new talk myweb talks new dune "Geometry Plans" # today; or -d 2026-12-01, -t topic This makes dune/<today>/geometry-plans/ with an org-beamer geometry-plans.org (using your setup.org ) and a draft talk.json , and opens the org file in your editor. Write the slides and export the PDF as usual ( C-c C-e l P ). Then: myweb talks refresh geometry-plans # title and pages from the org and PDF myweb talks refresh geometry-plans --publish --save # off draft, datalad save myweb deploy work Give it a summary, keywords and venue before publishing; the listing and search show them: myweb talks describe geometry-plans -e --save # all fields, in your editor This shows every field, set or not, as text: title: Geometry Plans subtitle: venue: url: keywords: Phlex, GDML summary: Two or three sentences, as many lines and paragraphs as you like. Change what you want, save and quit; an emptied field is cleared. Or set fields directly: -s "…" ( -s - reads stdin), -k per keyword, --title , --subtitle , --venue , --url . Use describe rather than editing talk.json by hand: for a migrated talk it also updates the talk's review, which migrating again (or pull ) writes talk.json from. Revisit a talk myweb talks edit geometry-plans # open its source # edit, re-export the PDF myweb talks refresh geometry-plans --save myweb deploy work Once a talk is in ~/keep/talks , edit it there, not in ~/sync/talks . Migrate a talk from ~/sync/talks myweb talks scan # find new and changed talks myweb talks resolve dune/topics/plans/plans --accept # an id from MIGRATION.org; migrates it datalad save -d ~/keep/talks -m "talks: migrate plans" myweb deploy work scan writes ~/keep/talks/MIGRATION.org , listing every candidate by its id (its path in ~/sync/talks , without extension). resolve --accept migrates that one as it is; add -d YYYY-MM-DD or -t topic if the scan guessed them wrong. Its title comes from the PDF; give the summary (and a better title, if need be) with myweb talks describe . For many talks at once, have reviews written from the digests ( myweb talks todo -p lists them, myweb talks fields describes a review), then myweb talks migrate --save . --reject and --material keep a candidate out. A migrated talk changed in ~/sync/talks myweb talks scan # shows it "changed", or "gone" if moved myweb talks pull shut-up-and-calculate --save # changed where it was myweb talks pull phlex-gdml-geometry \ --from ~/sync/talks/dune/topics/phlex/geom --save # moved, then changed myweb deploy work pull copies the talk's current files over the migrated ones and rewrites its talk.json . It keeps the talk's title, summary and keywords, and your audience , visibility , access and draft . The date and topic stay; a new group moves the talk, and so its URL. The geometry talk above was pulled this way, from wire-cell/ to dune/2026/11/20/ . Who sees a talk As for any item, by audience , visibility and access in talk.json , else the group's defaults under [talks.group.<name>] in myweb.toml (the edg group is protected), else [talks] . Talks are never sent to github. Artifacts Artifacts, like this page, are ready-made files served as they are. Make a directory under ~/keep/web/artifacts/ with the files and an artifact.toml : title = "Field response study" date = 2026-11-25 summary = "One line for the listing." tags = ["dune"] # entry = "report.html" if the page is not index.html # audience, visibility, access as for any item Then datalad save and deploy. To protect a whole tree with one password, nest artifacts in a group directory and set the group in myweb.toml : [artifacts.group.review] visibility = "protected" access = "review" # add review = "user review" to the target's realms drop: share files at expiring URLs drop copies files to tmp/ of the local or work web area and prints a URL. It never goes to github. drop put report.pdf # default target, ttl 7d, hashed URL drop put -t work --ttl 2w data/ fig.png drop put -t work --hash none -n slides deck.pdf # readable URL .../tmp/slides/ drop put -t work -u alice notes.pdf # password; new user gets one generated drop put -a -m "for the review" x.tgz # any user of the htpasswd drop put -y fig.png # also copy the URL to the clipboard Manage what is there: drop ls -A -l # all targets, with files and notes drop extend 3f9c2a 30d # new TTL from now, or "never" drop rm 3f9c2a # the id is the URL's last part drop gc -n # what has expired; without -n, remove it drop setup systemd # run gc hourly Users for password drops: drop passwd ls -t work drop passwd add -t work alice drop passwd prune -t work # offer to remove users no drop names Defaults (target, ttl, hash, index) are in ~/.config/drop/config.toml .
